title: Marshall Field's House (Artistic Houses, vol. 2 pt. 1, pp. 43–47)
creator: George William Sheldon (text); photographs uncredited (cf. LoC LC-DIG-ppmsca-56274/56275)
repository: Smithsonian Libraries (digitized on Internet Archive)
collection: George W. Sheldon, Artistic Houses (New York: D. Appleton, 1883–84), vol. 2 pt. 1 — Internet Archive item Artistichouses2
call_number: Artistic Houses v.2 pt.1 pp. 43–47 (IA leaves n52–n56)
rights_basis: Published 1883–84 in the United States; Internet Archive/Smithsonian Libraries scan
found_via: archive.org item Artistichouses2 (full text search 'Marshall Field'), leaf numbers located via the item's djvu.xml
notes: Contemporary (1883–84) description of the house exterior and plan — the best period text for the 1904 model: 'red pressed brick, with trimmings of light sandstone, three stories in height, with main entrance in the center of the west front, at the head of a broad flight of granite steps, a high porte-cochère on the northern side, and a fine large conservatory on the southern. Stables and other out-buildings are in the rear, on the side nearest the lake'; 'spacious lawn and scattered shade-trees' on the south side; vestibule floored in varied marbles; main hall runs the entire depth ending at a winding stairway under a large stained-glass window; reception room (right of hall) with a window into the conservatory (fountain); drawing-room left of hall; library behind it with fireplace at the east end; dining room opposite, glass doors into the conservatory. Field lived here until his death in Jan 1906, so the exterior description should still apply in 1904 (porte-cochère/conservatory survival to 1904 to be checked against the 1911 Sanborn).
